section_1.title: Introduction: The Smoothie Analogy (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a smoothie can be deconstructed back into its original fruit ingredients (strawberries, bananas, blueberries), a complex signal can be broken down into simple sine waves. Define the core objective: transforming data from the Time Domain to the Frequency Domain.
section_1.example: A chef blending fruits to create a smoothie; the Fourier Transform acts as the 'inverse blender' that tells you exactly how many grams of each fruit were used.

section_2.title: Prerequisites: The Language of Sine Waves (0:45-1:45)
section_2.content: Briefly review the parameters of a sine wave: Amplitude, Frequency, and Phase. Visualize these as rotating vectors (phasors) on a complex plane. This builds the foundational mental model for adding multiple waves together to create complex patterns (Superposition Principle).
section_2.example: A visual animation showing three simple sine waves of different frequencies stacking up to form a complex 'sawtooth' wave.

section_3.title: The Core Concept: The Rotating Windmill (1:45-3:15)
section_3.content: Explain the Fourier Transform as a mathematical 'sieve'. We multiply the signal by complex exponentials (rotating vectors) at different frequencies. When the 'rotation speed' matches a frequency hidden in the signal, the signal 'aligns' (constructive interference), creating a peak in the spectrum.
section_3.example: An animation of a 'spirograph' drawing: The signal wraps around a center point. If the winding frequency matches the signal frequency, the center of gravity shifts away from the origin, revealing the hidden component.

section_4.title: The Result: The Frequency Spectrum (3:15-4:15)
section_4.content: Explain the transition from a wave-form (Time Domain) to a 'Bar Chart' (Frequency Domain). Discuss how the peaks in the spectrum represent the 'DNA' of the signal, allowing us to filter noise or compress files.
section_4.example: An audio signal of a cat meowing. Show the messy wave in the time domain, then animate it snapping into a neat set of distinct bars on a frequency plot.

section_5.title: Conclusion & Real-World Application (4:15-5:00)
section_5.content: Summarize how this transformation allows us to manipulate signals—like removing high-frequency hiss from old recordings or compressing images (JPEG). End with the 'big picture': Everything in the universe is just a sum of vibrations.
section_5.example: A smartphone using Fourier Transform to perform 'Shazam'—identifying a song by matching its unique frequency fingerprint against a database.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Smoothies are complex signals composed of ingredients.",
            "Decompose the signal into simple sine waves.",
            "Time Domain shows waves over time.",
            "Frequency Domain shows the wave components.",
            "Transform data between these two domains."
        ]

        strawberry = Dot(color="#FF0000", radius=0.2)
        banana = Dot(color="#FFFF00", radius=0.2)
        smoothie = Circle(radius=0.7, color="#FF69B4").set_fill("#FF69B4", opacity=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(Create(self.place_at_grid(blender, 'C3')))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(strawberry, 'B2')),
            FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(banana, 'B4'))
